approved_story: More orders, harder next-basket prediction? What should a recommender forget?
prediction_task: next terminal basket repeat items within complete observed prior history; no next-order metadata
fixed_denominator: R_full=terminal products intersect entire observed historical product catalog; NEVER restrict labels/denominator/users when pruning candidates
factorial_primary_users: history_orders>=16 and nonempty R_full; same users in every cell
factorial_cells: ranking-information window recent5/all x eligible candidates recent5/all; complete historical catalog still known in all cells
history_observed_diagnostics: candidate count alone or candidate count x historical mean basket size; min cell counts10/20; raw overall, raw common support and standardized; no future target size for primary strata
future_target_conditioning: separate descriptive sensitivity only; never predictive input or evidence of causal history effect
dual_ranking: recent5 union top M old products by purchase_count descending, orders_since_purchase ascending, product_id ascending
matched_controls: same per-user candidate count as chosen dual; choose allhistory highest frequency or most recent products; no target labels
secondary_diagnostics: all predeclared M values with matched controls as descriptive confirmation curves, never reselect M; K5/20 for frozen policies; separate whole-basket scope and historical-product-group coverage
seed_aggregation: mean metrics and paired per-user recalls across three fitted model seeds; not ensemble predictions; intervals condition on fitted models
policy_selection: fewest average validation candidates among dual variants with paired 95% bootstrap lower Recall@10 delta vs full >= -0.005; ties higher recall then smaller M; full-catalog fallback allowed; descriptive validation search, independent confirmation required
multiplicity: paired user percentile bootstrap, marginal95 and Bonferroni simultaneous95 across9 contrasts
expansion_ledger: under identical frozen scores, new candidate true hits minus displaced old true hits equals total hits change; divide by R_full per user for additive recall contributions
product_groups: recent if age<5; dormant_repeat if age>=5 and purchase_count>=3; dormant_low_frequency otherwise; history-defined descriptive target coverage and hits
report_limits: algorithmic offline contrasts not human-behavior causal effects; no new algorithm/SOTA/online speed claim; condition intervals on fitted models and selected support
stop_rule: complete bounded validation, freeze, one fresh confirmation, independent audit, evidence report and story update; accept negative outcomes
